items.title: Joao Cancelo and Bruno Fernandes’ armband moment sparks controversy after Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal retirement
items.description:
A brief exchange after Portugal’s win over Wales has put Joao Cancelo, Bruno Fernandes and Cristiano Ronaldo at the center of attention. 
Portugal’s first victory since Cristiano Ronaldo stepped away from the national team came with an unexpected sequel off the pitch. A brief exchange between two of the squad’s leading figures, captured by television cameras once the match was over, has been picked apart by supporters ever since.



The moment took place in Cardiff on Tuesday, after Portugal edged Wales 3-2 in the Nations League. Goals from Bruno Fernandes, Pedro Neto and Carlos Forbs answered strikes by David Brooks and Sorba Thomas, and the result lifted Jorge Jesus’ side to the top of its group.



With Bernardo Silva, the new permanent captain, absent from the squad, Fernandes wore the armband and passed it to Joao Cancelo when he was substituted late in the match.



In footage broadcast on Sport TV after the final whistle, Fernandes pointed toward Cancelo and appeared to say “record him” to the cameraman. The full-back then pointed to the captain’s armband on his sleeve and said, “Film the boss,” according to Portuguese media, in what looked like a light-hearted moment.



pic.twitter.com/FHYsKdlQes— Goncalitosvid (@Goncalitosvid) November 18, 2026 



That has not stopped a portion of Ronaldo’s followers from reading it as a mockery. The timing explains part of the reaction, since the forward announced his international retirement on Nov. 5 after 234 appearances and 146 goals, having worn the armband for around two decades.



Several fans on X criticized both players and suggested the joke was aimed at Cristiano, while others simply saw an innocent bit of banter after a win that eased the sting of the 4-1 loss to Denmark.


        


Portugal secure a place in the Nations League quarter-finals



The win in Cardiff left Portugal at the top of their group, and as group winners, the reigning champions will be seeded in the draw for the quarter-finals, scheduled for Nov. 20 at UEFA’s headquarters. 



Teams from the same group cannot meet, so Norway is ruled out as a potential opponent, and Jorge Jesus’ side will be paired with one of the runners-up from the other three groups.



The possible rivals are Belgium, the Netherlands and Spain. The tie will be played over two legs, with first legs between March 25 and 27 and second legs between March 28 and 30, 2027.



For a group still adjusting to life without its all-time leading scorer, the draw will offer a first look at the road ahead. Whatever the outcome, the next international window in March will show whether the armband debate fades away or stays part of the conversation.

items.title: Ligue 1: sonorisation des arbitres à améliorer, hors-jeu semi-automatique... dans les coulisses de la VAR, qui cherche à faire l'unanimité
items.description: C'est dans une adresse tenue secrète que la Direction de l'arbitrage (DA) a accueilli RMC Sport pour une séance d'initiation à la VAR. Un exercice que la DA met en place dans une démarche pédagogique. Dans une grande salle remplie d'écrans, des arbitres et opérateurs revisionnent des milliers d'images chaque week-end de Ligue 1 pour éviter les erreurs. Aujourd'hui, la VAR est incontournable, parce qu'elle corrige "4 erreurs sur 5" selon les arbitres. Et si le bilan du début de saison est jugé "prometteur et encourageant" et qu'on se félicite du petit nombre de polémique, la VAR a encore une marge de progression. Tour d'horizon de ce qui peut permettre à cet outil d'être encore plus efficace.

items.title: Football : RMC Sport dans la peau d'un arbitre VAR
items.description:
Notre journaliste François Pinet est entré dans les coulisses de la VAR ! Dans un centre tenu secret, il a découvert puis testé le dispositif d’assistance vidéo utilisé par les arbitres du football français.

Pour cette immersion exceptionnelle, François Pinet a été accompagné par Bastien Dechepy, arbitre de Ligue 1. Installation du centre, communication avec les officiels, choix des images, ralentis et situations nécessitant une intervention : il lui explique chaque étape du processus.

Quand la VAR doit-elle intervenir ? Comment les arbitres analysent-ils une action litigieuse ? Qui prend la décision finale ? Cette visite permet de mieux comprendre un système souvent commenté, mais dont le fonctionnement précis reste largement méconnu du public.

Après la théorie, place à la pratique : installé devant les écrans, François Pinet se glisse dans la peau d’un arbitre vidéo et doit analyser plusieurs actions. Entre pression, angles multiples et décisions à prendre rapidement, l’exercice se révèle particulièrement exigeant.

Découvrez les coulisses de l’arbitrage vidéo et vivez cette expérience rare au cœur du centre VAR !

items.description: Mikel Oyarzabal ha convertido la camiseta de la selección española en su hábitat natural para el gol. El capitán de la Real Sociedad ha bajado el telón de los compromisos internacionales de 2026 consolidado como el gran referente ofensivo de Luis de la Fuente, cerrando el año natural con 10 tantos en su cuenta particular. Una cifra sobresaliente que le permite encadenar su tercer año consecutivo como máximo goleador de La Roja, confirmando una regularidad de élite absoluta en el panorama continental: firmó 6 dianas en un inolvidable 2024 -coronado con el histórico tanto decisivo en la final de la Eurocopa ante Inglaterra-, elevó el listón hasta las 9 en 2025 y este año ha dado un paso más allá alcanzando la decena. items.title: Lionel Messi earns Globe Soccer Awards nomination for Best Men’s Player, while Cristiano Ronaldo is left out again
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo head into the Globe Soccer Awards with very different outcomes. 
The Globe Soccer Awards have unveiled the shortlist for their 2026 edition, and the rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, the two players who defined an era, is once again part of the conversation. The best men’s player category has a familiar name returning and a notable absence, and the contrast says a lot about where each of them stands as the awards head to Dubai.



The Argentine forward is among the nominees, after a season in which he won his second straight MLS Golden Boot with 26 goals and 17 assists and led Inter Miami to the playoffs. Ronaldo, on the other hand, is not on the list of the main category, although he remains nominated for Best Middle East Player, an award he won last year.



Ousmane Dembele, Kylian Mbappe, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal are also among the contenders, and the winners will be announced on Dec. 28 in Dubai, with public voting open until Nov. 30.



The history of the awards explains why the names carry weight. Ronaldo is the most decorated player in the history of the Best Player category, with six wins in 2011, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019, and he has also received other honors, including the Player of the Century award for 2001-2020. Messi, in contrast, has won the Best Player award only once, in 2015, after a season in which he lifted the Champions League with Barcelona.




The nominees for Best Men's Player at the 2026 BEYOND Developments GLOBE SOCCER AwardsCongratulations to all the nominees.Vote for your finalists via the link in bio, at https://t.co/ZFEV3AEjn3, or on the Globe Soccer App. pic.twitter.com/upBO8mZFQ0— Globe Soccer Awards (@Globe_Soccer) November 18, 2026




Last year, neither of them was among the nominees for the top prize. Ronaldo was only nominated in the Middle East category, which he went on to win, while Messi did not appear in any category despite his MLS numbers, and Dembele ended up winning the Best Men’s Player award.



Full list of nominees for Best Men’s Player



Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid)Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona)Ousmane Dembele (Paris Saint-Germain)Federico Dimarco (Inter Milan)Desire Doue (Paris Saint-Germain)Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)Erling Haaland (Manchester City)Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain)Harry Kane (Bayern Munich)Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (Paris Saint-Germain)Lautaro Martinez (Inter Milan)Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)Lionel Messi (Inter Miami)Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain)Joao Neves (Paris Saint-Germain)Michael Olise (Bayern Munich)Raphinha (Barcelona)Declan Rice (Arsenal)Rodri (Manchester City)Fabian Ruiz (Paris Saint-Germain)Bukayo Saka (Arsenal)William Saliba (Arsenal)Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)Vinicius Jr. (Real Madrid)Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain)Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)



With voting open until Nov. 30, Messi will try to add a second Globe Soccer Best Player trophy to the one he won in 2015, in a field where he is the only nominee outside Europe, while Ronaldo waits on the Best Middle East Player award. The verdict in Dubai on Dec. 28 will add one more chapter to a rivalry that continues even after both stepped away from international soccer.

items.title: Didier Deschamps
items.description: Didier Deschamps, né le 15 octobre 1968 à Bayonne, est un des rares footballeur à avoir gagné la Coupe du monde comme joueur et comme sélectionneur. Originaire du Pays basque puis formé au FC Nantes, il évolue rapidement au poste de milieu défensif sous les couleurs nantaises mais il fait l'essentiel de sa carrière à Marseille puis Turin. Après 103 sélections en bleu, une Coupe du monde et un Euro, il devient entraîneur à l'AS Monaco où il atteint la finale de la Ligue des champions. Il remporte le titre de champion de Ligue 1 avec l'OM. Depuis 2012, il est le sélectionneur de l'équipe de France qu'il a mené au titre mondial en 2018. Il a quitté ses fonctions à l'issue de la Coupe du monde 2026, cédant sa place à Zinedine Zidane.

items.title: Argentina holds firm while Portugal drops a spot in the first FIFA ranking without Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo
items.description:
Argentina and Portugal take their first steps without Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, and the latest FIFA ranking shows that only one of them kept its place. 
The first FIFA ranking after the first international window without Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo is out, and it shows two national teams reacting differently to life without their biggest stars. Both Argentina and Portugal suffered a defeat in the November break, but the effect on the table was not the same for each.



Argentina remains in second place with 1,966.13 points, behind only Spain, which leads with 2,004.48. The Albiceleste lost 2-1 to Uruguay in its first match since Messi’s retirement, but it bounced back with a 7-0 win over Costa Rica to close the year, and it stays ahead of France (1,950.82) and England (1,938.90).



Portugal was less fortunate. The team dropped from fifth to sixth place with 1,801.28 points, after a 4-1 home loss to Denmark in a match that was supposed to honor Ronaldo’s retirement, but finished as the heaviest home defeat the team has suffered in more than a century.



It recovered with a 3-2 win over Wales to finish first in its Nations League group, but that was not enough to hold its spot, as Morocco climbed two places to fifth with 1,809.37 points, its highest position ever. Brazil also slipped one place, to seventh, with 1,800.91 points, only 0.37 behind the Portuguese.



FIFA Rankings. (inside.fifa.com)



What’s next for Argentina and Portugal after the ranking update



The next ranking update will arrive on Dec. 16, but it is unlikely to bring changes at the top of the table, since national teams will not play again until the first FIFA window of 2027, set for March 22-30. That means the positions of Argentina and Portugal could stay as they are for months, with both teams closing the year in places that reflect very different roads.


        


Argentina will return to action in March with one or two friendlies, as FIFA allows a maximum of two matches in that window and the federation has not yet started negotiations with any opponent.



European teams will be busy with the Nations League, so the Albiceleste would likely face rivals from other confederations. Portugal, for its part, will go back to the Nations League quarterfinals, and both Lionel Scaloni and Jorge Jesus will use the time to keep building squads without Messi and Ronaldo.

items.title: Marrero: "Por Remiro también soy lo que soy ahora, claro que me gustaría que siguiese"
items.description: Unai Marrero quiere más. Es lo que se saca en claro de su larga comparecencia este miércoles en Zubieta. Está contento con su progresión junto a Remiro, con Matarazzo apostando por él cada vez más. "Estoy tranquilo, centrado en mí mismo. Veo que estoy entrando a competir, cada vez más, soy un portero joven pero de gran ambición, la gente lo sabe. Sí quiero jugar más, claro, pero estoy en esa progresión, trabajando a tope, psicológicamente también muy bien. Peleando para tener más y más oportunidades. Entreno para ello, competimos bien y tengo ambición personal. Pero es competición y el entrenador tiene que elegir. Hay muchos partidos ahora, tengo que estar preparado, todos realmente. Todos vamos a ser importantes, siempre ha sido así", dijo.

items.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
items.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industryThe awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi
items.description: Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons. items.title: La Asociación Cultural El Caño de Vezdemarbán recauda 737 euros para la lucha contra el cáncer
items.description: La Asociación Cultural «El Caño de Vezdemarbán», entidad sin ánimo de lucro fundada en 2008 en la localidad zamorana de Vezdemarbán, y cuya labor se centra en impulsar la vida cultural, festiva y solidaria del municipio, ha hecho entrega de un donativo de 737 euros a la Asociación Española Contra el Cáncer (AECC) en su sede de Toro. La cantidad ha sido recaudada gracias a la marcha solidaria celebrada el pasado 31 de octubre en la localidad. La iniciativa reunió alrededor de un centenar de vecinos que participaron en un recorrido de dos kilómetros, pensado para que pudieran sumarse personas de todas las edades, desde los más pequeños hasta los mayores. Una vez finalizada la marcha, los asistentes compartieron un chocolate con churros en un ambiente de convivencia y solidaridad.

items.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
items.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and moreMail us with all of your questions and answers“The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?”The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017.183 places Montenegro (16th/199th)165 Kuwait (24/189)160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173)155 Cape Verde (27/182)153 Central African Republic (49/202)151 Libya (36/187)146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195)144 Moldova (37/181)141 El Salvador (49/190)136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

items.title: Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on
items.description: Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern gameThomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.Catch a falling star? Last month Grealish was suspended by Everton for three matches after “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it? items.title: Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs
items.description: The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the positionBy Opta AnalystOverlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.” Continue reading...

items.title: Mexico vs Jamaica: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Mexico vs Jamaica in the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League. Mexico host Jamaica in the Concacaf Nations League just days after the two sides met in a game that swung the wrong way for the hosts, and this rematch carries an obvious edge.
Mexico come into this one off a 2-3 loss to Jamaica on November 15, a result that saw them concede three goals at home and hand their rival a measure of belief heading into the return fixture. There is no earlier form listed beyond that defeat, which leaves Rafael Márquez’s side with little recent cushion to point to. A response is needed simply to steady the ship after that setback.
Jamaica arrive in good shape, having beaten Mexico 3-2 on November 15 before that they drew 1-1 with Honduras on October 6. Back to back results without a loss give Rudolph Speid’s group genuine confidence going into Mexican territory. A strong showing here would confirm Jamaica as a real threat in this Nations League cycle rather than a one-off upset side.
Mexico confirmed lineup
Márquez sends out a 4-3-3 built around Raúl Rangel in goal behind a back four of Rodrigo Huescas, Mateo Chávez, Israel Reyes and Jesús Orozco. Érik Lira anchors midfield alongside Álvaro Fidalgo, with Gilberto Mora given license to push forward from deep. Up top, Jesús Corona and Roberto Alvarado flank Julián Quiñones, giving Mexico width and pace to work with. There are no absences listed, so this looks close to a first-choice group tasked with avoiding a second straight loss to Jamaica.
Mexico confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Raúl Rangel, Rodrigo Huescas, Mateo Chávez, Érik Lira, Israel Reyes, Jesús Orozco, Gilberto Mora, Álvaro Fidalgo, Jesús Corona, Roberto Alvarado, Julián Quiñones. Coach: Rafael Márquez.
Jamaica confirmed lineup
Speid sticks with a 3-4-3, with Jahmali Waite in goal protected by Kyle Ming, Ronaldo Webster and Miguel Freckleton across the back. Richard King and Joël Latibeaudiere provide the central midfield platform, while Karoy Anderson and Courtney Clarke work the flanks in the four-man line. Javon East, Kaheim Dixon and Renaldo Cephas form the front three, the same attacking trio that did the damage in the last meeting. With no absences reported, Jamaica field a settled group looking to build on their recent win over this same opponent.
Jamaica confirmed starting XI (3-4-3): Jahmali Waite, Kyle Ming, Ronaldo Webster, Miguel Freckleton, Richard King, Joël Latibeaudiere, Karoy Anderson, Courtney Clarke, Javon East, Kaheim Dixon, Renaldo Cephas. Coach: Rudolph Speid.

items.title: Luis Suarez reveals how he sees his retirement alongside Lionel Messi, although it may not happen together
items.description:
Luis Suarez shared how he imagines the end of his career next to his longtime friend, but his answer suggests the finish line might not look the way many expect. 
Few friendships in soccer have lasted as long as the one between Luis Suarez and Lionel Messi, who first shared a dressing room at Barcelona and now do so again at Inter Miami.



With both in the final stretch of their careers, the question of how it will all end is starting to come up more and more, and Suarez gave his view on it in an interview with Catalunya Radio’s “Tot Costa” program.



The Uruguayan forward began by explaining that there is no set date and that the decision depends on the desire to keep competing. “It’s difficult, but well… As long as we keep having fun, enjoying ourselves and keep that competitive edge of wanting to win, of wanting to achieve things, neither he nor I nor everyone who has that ambition to keep achieving is going to stop,” he said.



Then came the part that points in another direction. Suarez imagined a moment in the future when their paths could split, because Messi, in his view, still has too much energy to stop. “There will come a time when he has so much energy, so much desire to keep playing that at some point I’m going to tell him: friend, everything is fine, you keep going, but I’ve come this far,” he explained with a laugh.



Lionel Messi and Luiz Suarez of Inter Miami. (Getty Images)



For now, he made it clear that both feel well. “As long as we’re fine, we’re happy, we’re enjoying ourselves and we look good physically, which is what people like, because one thing is to be there just to be there and another is to look good. On a personal level, I feel good, Leo is also fine, and that helps a lot,” Suarez said.



The forward, 39, has 17 goals and 8 assists in 32 matches this regular season, and his contract with Inter Miami expires at the end of the year, although he said talks to continue are underway.


        


Messi shows no signs of slowing down



While Suarez talks about the end of the road, Messi’s numbers say the Argentine is far from it. At 39, he led Inter Miami to the playoffs, with the team finishing second in the Eastern Conference, and closed the regular season with 26 goals and 17 assists, the best marks in the league in goals and in goal contributions (43). That earned him his second consecutive Golden Boot, which makes him the first player in MLS history to win it in back-to-back seasons.



Now he is also in the running for another record. Messi, who won the MVP award in 2024 and 2025, is one of five finalists for 2026 and is seen as the front-runner to become the first three-time winner in a row.



With numbers like these, it is easy to see why Suarez does not picture Messi stepping away anytime soon. Whether the two end up retiring together or not, the Argentine still has plenty to say on the pitch, starting with the playoffs, where Inter Miami will try to go for another title.

items.title: Argentina vs Costa Rica: Confirmed lineups for the 2026 international friendly game match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Argentina vs Costa Rica in a 2026 international friendly game. Argentina host Costa Rica in a 2026 international friendly that pits a World Cup winner’s squad against a Costa Rica side looking to find its footing ahead of next year.
Argentina come into this one off a 1-2 loss to Uruguay on November 13, a result that snapped a strong run that included a 3-0 win over Benin on October 6 and a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso two days before that. The gap between those lopsided wins and the defeat to Uruguay shows how much this Argentina squad can vary depending on personnel and opponent. A clean performance here would settle any lingering questions from that Uruguay setback.
Costa Rica arrive having lost 0-2 to Ecuador on November 14, their most recent outing on record. That result leaves Bryan Ruiz’s side searching for answers heading into this friendly. A positive showing against a team of Argentina’s caliber would mean far more than the scoreline alone.
Argentina confirmed lineup
Lionel Scaloni sends out a 4-3-3 built around Enzo Fernández and Alexis Mac Allister in midfield, with Máximo Perrone also in the engine room to help control possession. Julián Alvarez and Nico Paz support Gianluca Prestianni up front, giving Argentina pace and movement across the frontline. At the back, Emiliano Martínez starts in goal behind a line of Agustín Giay, Román Vega, Lisandro Martínez and Facundo Medina. There are no absences listed for Argentina, so Scaloni has his full group of selected players to work with.
Argentina confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Emiliano Martínez, Agustín Giay, Román Vega, Máximo Perrone, Lisandro Martínez, Facundo Medina, Enzo Fernández, Alexis Mac Allister, Julián Alvarez, Nico Paz, Gianluca Prestianni. Coach: Lionel Scaloni.
Costa Rica confirmed lineup
Bryan Ruiz lines Costa Rica up in a 4-1-4-1, with Celso Borges holding in front of the back four to shield Francisco Calvo, Juan Vargas, Kenyel Michel and Gerald Taylor. Andrey Soto, Carlos Mora, Aarón Salazar and Josimar Méndez make up a busy midfield four tasked with supporting lone striker Manfred Ugalde. Patrick Sequeira starts in goal behind that setup. Costa Rica have no absences listed, meaning Ruiz can call on his intended group against a tough Argentina side.
Costa Rica confirmed starting XI (4-1-4-1): Patrick Sequeira, Kenyel Michel, Gerald Taylor, Celso Borges, Juan Vargas, Francisco Calvo, Carlos Mora, Aarón Salazar, Manfred Ugalde, Andrey Soto, Josimar Méndez. Coach: Bryan Ruiz.

items.title: Al Nassr reportedly eyeing a historic father-son moment with Cristiano Ronaldo and Cristiano Jr
items.description:
Al Nassr is reportedly exploring a special scenario for Cristiano Ronaldo and his teenage son, one that would add a new chapter to the veteran forward’s career. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has spent more than two decades chasing records and trophies, but a different kind of milestone could be waiting for him in Saudi Arabia. After closing his international career with Portugal, the forward may still have one more special moment to live, this time at club level.



Al Nassr is reportedly working so that Ronaldo and his son can play together with the first team in 2027, according to Saudi journalist Tariq Al-Nofal. The club had already been linked to that idea in April, when Saudi outlet Al Wiam reported that it was considering inviting Cristiano Jr. to train with the senior squad next season, a plan that now appears to be getting closer.



The report arrives at a moment of growth for the young forward. The 16-year-old has stood out in Al Nassr’s youth ranks and has earned a place with Portugal’s youth national teams.



His rise reached a new stage shortly after his father’s retirement from Portugal, as he made his debut with the under-17 team, coming off the bench in the 73rd minute of a Euro 2027 qualifier against Andorra.



🚨| Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. delivers an amazing performance for Portugal U17! 🇵🇹🔥He’s clearly following in his father’s footsteps. 🐐 pic.twitter.com/ccwawoyA99— Kalshi EPL (@KalshiEPL) November 12, 2026 



Ronaldo, 41, is under contract with Al Nassr until June 2027, the same month in which Cristiano Jr. turns 17, so the timing of any shared appearance would depend on the teenager’s development and on the club’s sporting decisions in the coming months.



The plan could also serve Al Nassr beyond the pitch: with his contract nearing its end, the prospect of playing alongside his son could become a strong argument for convincing Ronaldo to extend his stay in Saudi Arabia.


        


Could Lionel Messi share the pitch with his son too?



The idea inevitably raises a question about Lionel Messi, who could be next in line for a similar scene. His eldest son, Thiago, turned 14 on Nov. 2 and plays for Inter Miami’s under-14 team, with which he won the MIC Football Punta Cana tournament in June.



The age gap also makes the comparison different: Thiago is two years younger than Cristiano Jr., so any chance of a father-son appearance for Messi would be further away and would depend on how long the Argentine, 39, continues playing and on how the teenager develops at the youth level.



For now, only Ronaldo’s case has emerged as a real possibility, since there are no reports of a similar plan for Messi and his son. Even so, the idea remains a report without official confirmation, and whether it becomes reality will depend on time, on Cristiano Jr.’s progress and on a decision from Ronaldo himself about how long he wants to keep playing.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have company as Harry Kane joins elite Ballon d’Or list with goal against Spain
items.description:
The England captain's latest achievement puts him alongside some of the game's biggest legends, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, following a dramatic night in Madrid. 
Harry Kane has added his name to another exclusive chapter in soccer history after a memorable performance against Spain. The England captain’s latest achievement puts him alongside some of the game’s biggest legends, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, following a dramatic night in Madrid.



England claimed a 3-2 victory over Spain in the UEFA Nations League last Sunday, ending the reigning world champions’ remarkable unbeaten run. Kane played a decisive role, scoring from the penalty spot just before half-time to give Thomas Tuchel’s side the lead.



Thomas Tuchel’s players started brightly at the Metropolitano Stadium, pressing La Roja aggressively and preventing the home side from finding its usual rhythm. Kane won a penalty after being fouled by Pau Cubarsi and calmly converted it in the final moments of the first half, registering his 93rd international goal for England.



The visitors carried their momentum into the second half, with Ezri Konsa doubling the lead before Ben White made it 3-0 after a well-worked attacking move involving Jude Bellingham. England appeared to be heading towards a comfortable victory, but the match took a dramatic turn when Elliot Anderson was sent off for denying Lamine Yamal a goalscoring opportunity.









Spain took advantage of its numerical superiority, with Mikel Oyarzabal converting the resulting penalty before Nico Williams made it 3-2. However, James Trafford produced crucial saves late in the match to help England hold on and secure first place in its Nations League group.



Kane joins Messi and Ronaldo



Beyond the result, Kane’s goal carried a significant individual milestone. Soccer statistician MisterChip has revealed that the Bayern striker became the fifth reigning Ballon d’Or winner to score against Spain.



The list stretches back to 1984, when Michel Platini scored against Spain in the European Championship final. Roberto Baggio followed in the 1994 World Cup quarter-final, before Lionel Messi found the net against La Roja in a friendly in September 2010.



Harry Kane of England scores from the penalty spot against Spain



Cristiano Ronaldo became the fourth player to achieve the feat when he scored a hat-trick against Spain at the 2018 World Cup, with Kane now completing the exclusive group after his Nations League penalty. The five players and their respective matches are:



DatePlayerCountryCompetition27.06.1984Michel PlatiniFranceEuro final09.07.1994Roberto BaggioItalyWorld Cup quarter-final07.09.2010Lionel MessiArgentinaFriendly15.06.2018Cristiano RonaldoPortugalWorld Cup group stage (hat-trick)15.11.2026Harry KaneEnglandNations League group stageReigning Ballon d’Or winners to score against Spain



Kane’s inclusion adds another remarkable achievement to a career that has already seen him become England’s all-time leading goalscorer. He also joins Ronaldo and Messi in a statistic that highlights how rarely the reigning Ballon d’Or winner manages to score against Spain.

items.title: Why is Cristiano Ronaldo not playing for Portugal vs Wales in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 6?
items.description:
Portugal faces Wales without Cristiano Ronaldo, following a heavy defeat suffered against Denmark. 
Portugal closes its Nations League group stage on Tuesday against Wales at Cardiff City Stadium, and the team sheet once again does not include the name Cristiano Ronaldo.



The reason for Ronaldo’s absence is that he is no longer part of the national team. The 41-year-old retired from international soccer on Nov. 5, ending a run of 234 appearances and 146 goals, both all-time records for his country and the world.



What is new is how Portugal got here. The team was beaten 4-1 by Denmark in Braga on Saturday, in a night that was supposed to honor Ronaldo and instead turned into the heaviest home defeat the team has suffered in more than a century.



Denmark was 4-0 up before Bernardo Silva scored a late goal, and Jesus took responsibility afterward. “If the team couldn’t do it, it has to do with my instructions,” the coach said. When asked if he misses Ronaldo, he replied: “How can I miss him when he is no longer in the national team?”




Fechar a fase de grupos com uma 𝙫𝙞𝙩𝙤́𝙧𝙞𝙖. ☝️🇵🇹 #NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/XdlwjDhxIT— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 17, 2026




The atmosphere in Braga reflected a mix of nostalgia and frustration. As parts of the crowd began to leave before the final whistle, some supporters chanted Ronaldo’s name, a sign that the farewell was still fresh even though the team failed to deliver on the pitch. 



Jesus acknowledged that feeling but made it clear that the page has been turned. “People miss him and have not forgotten what Cristiano did for 23 years with the national team, but there is no going back on the matter,” he said.


        


What is at stake for Portugal after the loss to Denmark



Even after the heavy defeat, Portugal’s situation is far from critical. The team had already booked a place in the quarterfinals thanks to four straight wins to open the campaign, so what remains in play is finishing at the top of Group A4. 



A point in Cardiff would be enough to secure it, while a slip could open the door for Denmark, which would pass Portugal by beating Norway on the same night.



The task will not be simple for Jesus, who has to rebuild his lineup with several names missing. Ruben Dias and Joao Palhinha are serving suspensions, and Bernardo Silva was ruled out as unfit after scoring Portugal’s lone goal against Denmark.



Portugal now has a chance to answer in Cardiff, in a match that can reset its direction after a tough week. With Ronaldo already gone from the national team, Jesus needs a response from his players to close the group stage as a winner.

items.title: Wales vs Portugal: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Wales vs Portugal in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. Wales host Portugal at a stage of this Nations League campaign where both sides are still searching for answers on defense, and that shared problem should shape how this one is played.
Wales come into this match on the back of two straight defeats, falling 1-3 to Norway on November 14 after a 0-1 loss to Denmark back on October 4. The goals have dried up and the results have followed a similar pattern of narrow or lopsided losses. A result here matters for Craig Bellamy’s side simply to stop the losing run before it becomes a longer slide.
Portugal arrive having split their last two outings, beaten 1-4 by Denmark on November 14 just weeks after edging Norway 2-1 on October 4. That Denmark scoreline stands out as a heavy defeat for a squad of this quality, and it puts extra weight on how Jorge Jesus sets his team up here. A win would steady things after that result and keep Portugal’s campaign on track.
Wales confirmed lineup
Bellamy sets Wales up in a 4-4-2 with Karl Darlow behind a back line of Connor Roberts, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies and Jay DaSilva. The midfield pairing of Daniel James and Rubin Colwill on the flanks alongside Brennan Johnson, Lewis Koumas and Harry Wilson is built to supply the front two, with Liam Cullen leading the line. There are no listed absences, so this looks like the strongest group Bellamy has available, and the shape suggests Wales will look to get numbers forward quickly rather than sit back against a stronger side.
Wales confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Danny Ward, Connor Roberts, Jay Dasilva, David Brooks, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Daniel James, Josh Sheehan, Rubin Colwill, Harry Wilson, Sorba Thomas. Coach: Craig Bellamy.
Portugal confirmed lineup
Jesus goes with a 4-2-3-1, with Diogo Costa in goal and a back four of Diogo Dalot, Renato Veiga, António Silva and João Cancelo. Rúben Neves and Vítor Vitinha sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Bruno Fernandes, Pedro Neto and João Félix behind lone striker Gonçalo Ramos. With no absences listed, Portugal field a full-strength XI, and the balance between Neves and Vitinha should let Fernandes push forward and link with Félix and Ramos in the final third.
Portugal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Diogo Costa, Diogo Dalot, João Cancelo, Vitinha, António Silva, Renato Veiga, Trincão, João Neves, Gonçalo Ramos, Bruno Fernandes, Pedro Neto. Coach: Jorge Fernando Pinheiro de Jesus.

items.title: Antoine Griezmann pays tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo: ‘What he has done for Portugal is historic’
items.description:
Antoine Griezmann has shared an emotional message for Cristiano Ronaldo, a longtime rival who he says leaves a huge void in Portugal. 
Antoine Griezmann has joined the long list of voices reacting to Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement from international football, and his words carry the weight of someone who spent years competing against him.



The Frenchman shared his thoughts during a press conference with Orlando City, where he looked back on what the Portuguese star meant to the game, admitting that the news hit him. “I am sad about Cristiano’s retirement. He is an absolute legend, a machine when it comes to working, scoring goals and winning,” he told reporters.



His praise then focused on Ronaldo’s impact on his country, along with the void he leaves behind. “I really enjoyed playing against him, and the truth is that what he has done for Portugal is historic. He will be very difficult to replace,” Griezmann added.



Ronaldo brought his international career to an end on Nov. 5, when he decided to step aside amid tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus. The Portuguese legend leaves behind impressive numbers, with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both world records at the national team level.



🐐🔥 CRISTIANO RONALDO HAS A HIGH-PROFILE ADMIRER!🇫🇷⚽ Antoine Griezmann made no secret of his admiration for CR7 following the announcement of his retirement from international football, praising the greatness of the Portuguese legend👀 Do you consider Cristiano Ronaldo the… pic.twitter.com/HjuIzDxi4k— beIN SPORTS USA (@beINSPORTSUSA) November 17, 2026 



A rivalry that started in LaLiga



Most of the duels between Ronaldo and Griezmann took place in LaLiga, where the Frenchman faced the Real Madrid star while wearing the colors of Real Sociedad and, later, Atletico Madrid. Their paths in Spain stopped crossing when Griezmann moved to Barcelona in 2019, since Ronaldo had already left Madrid for Juventus a year earlier.


        


The two also met at the international level, with the most memorable encounter coming in the Euro 2016 final. Portugal beat France in that match, and the victory gave Ronaldo the first major title of his career with the national team.



Their last meeting came on July 5, 2024, in the quarterfinals of Euro 2024. The match ended 0-0 after extra time, and Portugal advanced on penalties, closing the rivalry between two players who defined an era for their countries.



Griezmann’s words show the respect that remained between two players who spent years on opposite sides of some of football’s biggest stages. With Ronaldo gone from the international scene, Portugal now faces the challenge of moving forward without its all-time icon, while Griezmann continues his career in MLS with Orlando City.

items.description: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the jobThe Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. items.title: Lionel Scaloni opens the door for Lionel Messi to join Argentina’s coaching staff for the 2030 World Cup
items.description:
Lionel Scaloni joked about a future role for Lionel Messi on Argentina’s bench, with an unexpected vacancy in the staff as the backdrop. 
Lionel Scaloni was asked about a scenario many Argentina fans have probably imagined since Lionel Messi retired from the national team: seeing the captain on the sidelines instead of on the pitch.



The head coach addressed it at the press conference ahead of the friendly against Costa Rica, the last match of the November international window, and his answer was a mix of humor and honesty.



Scaloni first made it clear that he doesn’t see Messi leaving the pitch anytime soon. “I think he’s going to keep playing. He’s going to keep playing beyond 2030. He already said no with the national team, but as a player, I hope he continues,” the coach said.



When the question turned to a possible role on the bench, Scaloni used the situation of Walter Samuel, who is leaving the staff after the Costa Rica match, to joke about it. “If he wants to come, there’s no problem. Now that Walter (Samuel) is gone, look… let him come,” he said with a smile.




👀🇦🇷 Lionel Scaloni on Leo Messi in the coaching staff for World Cup 2030: “I think Messi will still be playing football beyond 2030!”.“But now that Walter Samuel is leaving, he’s welcome whenever he wants”, he said smiling. 😁 pic.twitter.com/HSYmZo3pdB— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 17, 2026




Messi retired from the national team on Aug. 31, at 39, through a letter and a video that looked back at his career with the Albiceleste. His farewell in front of the home crowd came on Oct. 6 at the Monumental, in a 3-0 win over Benin in which he scored from the penalty spot and also assisted Nicolas Otamendi and Nicolas Paz. The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner leaves behind a huge legacy with 208 appearances, 126 goals and 67 assists, all of them records for Argentina.



Scaloni is confirmed for 2030 World Cup


        


Scaloni’s future was already settled before the comment about Messi. The Argentine Football Association announced on Nov. 12 that the coach extended his deal to lead the national team through the 2030 World Cup, with AFA president Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia presenting the news alongside him at a press conference. 



The agreement covers the 2027-2030 cycle and puts to rest the doubts about his continuity after Argentina fell to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The renewal also includes most of his staff, among them Pablo Aimar, who will remain through 2030 as well. The only exception is Samuel, who is leaving the setup to begin his own path as a head coach.



Scaloni’s new deal also puts him on course for a milestone no Argentine coach has reached. After guiding the team to the title in Qatar in 2022 and to the final in 2026, he will become the first Argentine manager to lead the national team in three different World Cups once the 2030 edition arrives.



For now, Messi’s name on the staff remains only a joke, and his focus appears to be on continuing as a player with Inter Miami. What is clear is that Scaloni will be on the bench through 2030, with the chance to keep writing his name in Argentina’s history book.

items.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparationsI was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. items.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
items.description: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records. Continue reading...

items.title: Canada vs Guatemala: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Canada vs Guatemala in the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League. Canada and Guatemala meet again just days after their last meeting, with both camps naming unchanged-look lineups for the rematch in this Concacaf Nations League fixture.
Canada come into this one off a 3-2 win over this same Guatemala side on November 14, a result that showed they can get the job done even when they do not shut the door defensively. That match also marked their most recent outing, so Mauro Biello’s group will look to carry the same attacking edge into this second meeting. Another result here would keep Canada’s momentum rolling in this Nations League cycle.
Guatemala head into this match on the back of a 2-3 loss to Canada on November 14, a game in which they scored twice but still came up short. Before that, they had beaten Suriname 1-0 on October 6, showing they can grind out low-scoring wins when needed. Luis Fernando Tena’s side will be looking to flip the script against the same opponent and respond with a better result this time.
Canada confirmed lineup
Canada line up in a 4-4-2 with Maxime Crépeau behind a back line of Niko Sigur, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman and Richie Laryea. Mathieu Choinière and Nathan Saliba sit in midfield alongside wide options Tajon Buchanan and Liam Millar, giving Biello’s side width and the ability to get bodies forward quickly. Jonathan David partners Tani Oluwaseyi up front, pairing David’s finishing with Oluwaseyi’s movement. There are no absences to account for, so Canada field what looks like their strongest available group.
Canada confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Maxime Crépeau, Niko Sigur, Richie Laryea, Mathieu Choinière, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman, Tajon Buchanan, Nathan Saliba, Tani Oluwaseyi, Jonathan David, Liam Millar. Coach: Mauro Biello.
Guatemala confirmed lineup
Guatemala also set up in a 4-4-2, with Kenderson Navarro in goal protected by Aarón Herrera, Nicolás Samayoa, Allen Yanes and José Morales across the back. Rodrigo Saravia and José Rosales anchor the midfield while Óscar Santis and Jesús López provide width to support the front line. Rubio Rubín and Jehú Fajardo lead the attack, with Tena asking his front two to work off service from the flanks. With no absences listed, Guatemala are able to pick from a full squad for this rematch.
Guatemala confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Kenderson Navarro, Aarón Herrera, José Morales, Rodrigo Saravia, Allen Yanes, Nicolás Samayoa, Óscar Santis, José Rosales, Rubio Rubín, Jehú Fajardo, Jesús López. Coach: Luis Fernando Tena.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi set the standard as Vinicius reveals why matching GOATs’ consistency is so difficult amid Real Madrid struggles
items.description:
The Brazilian forward has faced increased scrutiny during a difficult start to the current campaign, but his latest comments offer insight into how he views expectations placed on modern players. 
Vinicius Junior has opened up about the pressure of maintaining elite performances at Real Madrid, reflecting on the remarkable standards set by Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi. The Brazilian forward has faced increased scrutiny during a difficult start to the current campaign, but his latest comments offer insight into how he views expectations placed on modern players.



With his performances attracting attention ahead of international duty with Brazil, Vinicius has acknowledged the challenge of remaining at the highest level throughout an entire career. The Real Madrid star also addressed the factors behind his recent struggles, while making clear that he remains determined to improve.



The Brazil international has endured a quieter opening to the 2026-27 season than many would have expected, recording one goal and three assists in 12 La Liga appearances. His output has attracted criticism as Real Madrid looks to maintain its position among the leading contenders in Spain.



Several factors have reportedly contributed to his slower start, including limited preparation time following the 2026 World Cup, transfer speculation and a four-match suspension in La Liga. Those circumstances have disrupted his rhythm, although the Brazilian remains an important part of Los Blancos’ attacking plans.



Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid (2026)



Pressure of performing at highest level



The discussion around the 26-year-old forward comes amid the enormous expectations placed on players who become the faces of major clubs and national teams. His performances are frequently compared with those of soccer’s greatest forwards, making consistency a particularly important part of the conversation.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi spent years producing extraordinary numbers season after season, setting a benchmark that few players have managed to approach. Vinicius recognizes the difficulty of sustaining that level, particularly in an era when players are constantly judged on their latest performances.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal shakes hands with Lionel Messi of Argentina



Vinicius explains why Ronaldo and Messi are different



Speaking ahead of Brazil’s international commitments, Vinicius addressed the comparisons and explained why maintaining such extraordinary consistency is an exceptional achievement. He singled out Ronaldo and Messi as the only players he believes managed to produce the same level of numbers over so many years.



“Staying at such a high level for so long is very difficult. I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi managed to do it for so many years, consistently putting up the same numbers,” Vinicius said at a press conference.



💬 Vinicius: "Solo Cristiano Ronaldo y Messi han mantenido su nivel durante tantos años" 🗣️ "Soy humano y fallo muchas veces. En el momento más decisivo de la temporada siempre estoy ahí" pic.twitter.com/sR3xEtETJI— Mundo Deportivo (@mundodeportivo) November 16, 2026 



The Brazilian also reminded critics that he is still learning and cannot be expected to deliver perfect performances every time he steps onto the pitch. “I’m human, and I make mistakes many times, but I’m always trying to improve. Nevertheless, I am still 26 years old, and I have the right to enjoy life a little too,” he added.



His comments reflect an understanding of the demands that come with playing for Real Madrid, where expectations remain exceptionally high regardless of a player’s age or previous achievements. Vinicius is determined to improve while also recognizing the importance of finding a balance between soccer and his personal life.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo was not deceived as Jorge Jesus singles out what he promised Portugal’s legend before joining him at Al-Nassr
items.description:
The national team coach has addressed their time working together at Al-Nassr, revisiting a promise that has taken on added significance amid the recent controversy surrounding Ronaldo’s departure. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement continues to dominate the headlines in Portugal, with Jorge Jesus now offering a fresh insight into his relationship with the former captain. The national team coach has addressed their time working together at Al-Nassr, revisiting a promise that has taken on added significance amid the recent controversy surrounding Ronaldo’s departure.



Jesus’ comments come after Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, accused Portugal of failing to appreciate her son, while the national team attempts to move forward following a disappointing start to life without its all-time leading scorer. The coach has maintained that Ronaldo’s legacy remains unquestionable, despite the tensions that surrounded the final months of his international career.



Aveiro recently launched a public attack on Portugal following its 4-1 defeat to Denmark, the first match since Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5. Speaking during a ceremony at Sporting’s José Alvalade Stadium, she claimed her son had been deceived and suggested he had not received the respect he deserved.



“Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I’m sad too,” she said, before admitting she was pleased with the Selecao’s defeat because she believed the result was deserved. She also criticized the tribute organized for Ronaldo in Braga, insisting it should have taken place in his presence rather than after his departure.



😳🇵🇹 LA MADRE DE CRISTIANO RONALDO, DURÍSIMA CONTRA PORTUGAL:“La derrota contra Dinamarca estaba BIEN MERECIDA, ESTABA CONTENTA POR ELLO. El homenaje debería haberse realizado en su presencia. Es aquí, en el Sporting, donde le vamos a rendir homenaje. Aquí se reconoce su…— Ataque Futbolero (@AtaqueFutbolero) November 16, 2026 



Ronaldo’s relationship with Jesus came under scrutiny



The controversy surrounding Ronaldo’s exit is closely connected to his relationship with Jesus, who previously coached him at Al-Nassr before taking charge of Portugal. Tensions reportedly developed over the forward’s involvement and playing time, with Ronaldo eventually leaving the national team camp during the October international window.



Jesus has defended his decisions as those of a manager acting in the team’s interests, insisting that no individual player should dictate his approach. The situation has attracted further attention following Aveiro’s accusations, but the coach has now offered a more personal account of his connection with the Portuguese superstar.



Head coach Jorge Jesus interacts with Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr



Jesus reveals what he promised Ronaldo at Al-Nassr



Speaking ahead of Portugal’s Nations League match against Wales, Jesus described Ronaldo as a lasting icon of Portuguese soccer and recalled the commitment he made when joining Al-Nassr. The coach insisted he had kept his word and had never deceived the forward about his intentions.



“Cris is a legend of Portuguese football. The Portuguese national team and Portuguese football will never be able to forget him,” Jesus said. He then explained: “As his friend, I worked with him for a year, and I got to know him personally. When I went to Al-Nassr, I told him: ‘I’m going there, and I’ll help you become champions.’ I didn’t deceive him.”



🚨 𝐉𝐎𝐑𝐆𝐄 𝐉𝐄𝐒𝐔𝐒: "𝐀𝐒 𝐇𝐈𝐒 𝐅𝐑𝐈𝐄𝐍𝐃, 𝐈 𝐖𝐎𝐑𝐊𝐄𝐃 𝐖𝐈𝐓𝐇 𝐇𝐈𝐌 𝐅𝐎𝐑 𝐀 𝐘𝐄𝐀𝐑"🇵🇹🗣 Jorge Jesus:"Cris is a legend of Portuguese football. The Portuguese national team and Portuguese football will never be able to forget him.As his friend, I worked…— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 16, 2026 



Jesus also acknowledged that Ronaldo’s international departure is now a reality that Portugal must accept. “The situation is a reality. We all know it and are prepared for it,” he added, making clear that the squad has to concentrate on its future rather than remain caught up in the controversy.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s absence no longer a leadership problem for Portugal as Ruben Neves reveals who will step up
items.description:
The midfielder has addressed the ongoing discussion surrounding the former captain, offering an insight into the atmosphere inside the dressing room and explaining why the squad remains confident despite the constant attention. 
Cristiano Ronaldo‘s international retirement has left Portugal facing questions about its future, but Ruben Neves believes the national team has enough experience and leadership to move forward. The midfielder has addressed the ongoing discussion surrounding the former captain, offering an insight into the atmosphere inside the dressing room and explaining why the squad remains confident despite the constant attention.



Ronaldo’s departure has continued to dominate press conferences, with Portugal’s performances regularly being compared to the period when the legendary forward was part of the team. Neves, however, insists that the situation has not disrupted the squad’s unity or affected its performances on the pitch.



The midfielder believes the continued media attention is the main reason the subject remains prominent. Speaking about when the discussion might finally disappear, Neves suggested that the focus needs to shift back towards football. “As for when this will end, I think it will end when the questions and interviews about this topic stop. Cristiano himself put an end to it by issuing an official statement,” the 29-year-old explained to reporters, via Sport TV.



He also acknowledged that the veteran’s status makes the questions understandable, but hopes the players will eventually be able to concentrate on their responsibilities without repeatedly discussing the former captain. According to Neves, the external attention has not affected the team’s atmosphere or performances.



Rúben Neves: "Foi o próprio Cristiano a colocar um ponto final e a fazer um comunicado quando terminou a sua participação na Seleção" pic.twitter.com/sJegp0AwGW— Cabine Desportiva (@CabineSport) November 16, 2026 



Portugal insists Ronaldo’s departure has not affected team harmony



Neves was particularly keen to dismiss suggestions that the constant debate has created problems within the dressing room. The Al-Hilal midfielder explained that the positive atmosphere he has experienced throughout his years with Portugal remains unchanged. “This external noise doesn’t affect us at all; it doesn’t have any impact on our performance or the atmosphere within our group,” he said. 



He added that the team spirit and harmony have remained consistent since he first joined the national setup. The midfielder also acknowledged that the squad remains grateful for everything Ronaldo contributed during his international career. However, he believes the responsibility now belongs to the players who continue representing Portugal.



Ruben Neves and Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal acknowledge the fans



“Cristiano released a statement when he ended his international career. We are forever grateful to him for everything he gave. But we understand that the responsibility now lies with us, and we must represent the national team and bear that responsibility,” Neves said.



Neves reveals who will take over Portugal’s leadership role



With Ronaldo no longer part of the squad, questions have naturally emerged about who will become the team’s main dressing-room figures. Neves believes Portugal has several experienced players capable of sharing those responsibilities rather than relying on one individual to replace the former captain.



“It’s normal; there are leaders, and luckily we have several. The more experienced players are trying to help the younger players. The atmosphere is great, and there are many players capable of taking on that role,” he explained.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Ruben Neves 



Neves also highlighted the importance of helping younger players adapt to international soccer, insisting that the transition has happened naturally. “Fortunately, our national team has many players with leadership qualities, so it’s a natural fit for us and the team as a whole,” he added.



He believes the squad has enough experience to guide the next generation, making Ronaldo’s departure less of a leadership concern than some outside observers suggest. The midfielder’s comments indicate that responsibility will be shared across the dressing room rather than transferred to a single successor.

items.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managersSign up for our free newsletter hereWho should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom SAlthough the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. items.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
items.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreakLast week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result.Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. items.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
items.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL drawSonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. items.title: France vs Turkey: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for France vs Turkey in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. France and Turkey meet in the Nations League with the hosts looking to settle after a rocky November and the visitors still searching for any kind of result to build on.
France come into this one off a 1-3 loss to Italy on November 12, a result that snapped the momentum they built from a 4-1 win over Belgium on October 5 and a 1-1 draw with Italy on October 2. The dip against Italy stung, but the Belgium result showed what this group can do when the attack clicks. A win here would go a long way toward steadying the ship before the next international window.
Turkey arrive having lost all three of their last outings, falling 1-2 to Belgium on November 12 after a 1-3 defeat to Italy on October 5 and a 0-3 loss to Belgium on October 2. The pattern is clear: Turkey have struggled to find the net or keep games close against top opposition. This match is a chance to avoid a fourth straight defeat and show some sign of progress.
France confirmed lineup
France are set up in a 4-3-3 with Mike Maignan behind a back line of Jeremy Jacquet, Ibrahima Konate, Adrien Truffert and Andy Diouf in a fullback role. The midfield trio of Eduardo Camavinga, Lucas Da Cunha and Warren Zaire-Emery gives the side balance between ball retention and running power, while Michael Olise, Kylian Mbappe and Bradley Barcola form an attacking front three with real pace and goal threat. There are no listed absences, so France should field close to a full-strength group, and the challenge will be converting their attacking talent into the kind of control that was missing against Italy.
France confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Mike Maignan, Saël Kumbedi, Andy Diouf, Lucas da Cunha, Jérémy Jacquet, Ibrahima Konaté, Rayan Cherki, Adrien Rabiot, Kylian Mbappé, Michael Olise, Bradley Barcola. Coach: Zinedine Zidane.
Turkey confirmed lineup
Turkey line up in a 4-2-3-1, with Berke Ozer in goal behind Zeki Celik, Merih Demiral, Abdulkerim Bardakci and Ferdi Kadioglu. Salih Ozcan and Orkun Kokcu sit as the double pivot, screening for a front four of Arda Guler, Yunus Akgun and Baris Alper Yilmaz behind lone striker Enes Unal. With no absences listed, this is close to the strongest group available, and the shape is built to stay compact and look to Guler and Unal for a spark going forward. Turkey will need more composure on the ball than in recent games if they hope to avoid another lopsided scoreline.
Turkey confirmed starting XI (5-3-2): Berke Özer, Zeki Çelik, Eren Elmali, Emirhan Topçu, Abdülkerim Bardakci, Merih Demiral, Ismail Yüksek, Hakan Çalhanoğlu, Deniz Gül, Arda Güler, Can Uzun. Coach: Sergen Yalçin.

items.title: Spain vs England: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Spain vs England in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. Spain and England meet in the Nations League with both unbeaten through their last three outings, a matchup between two of the group’s in-form sides.
Spain come into this one having won all three of their last matches, beating Czechia 2-0 on November 12 after earlier wins over Croatia and Czechia in October. The run has been built on control in midfield and quick finishing, with La Fuente’s side yet to drop points across that stretch. A win here would keep Spain firmly in charge of their group standing.
England arrive on the back of an even more emphatic run, including a 7-0 win over Croatia on October 3 and a 3-0 win over Czechia three days later, before closing with a 2-1 win against Croatia on November 12. Tuchel’s side have scored freely in all three games and have shown no signs of easing off. This match is a chance for England to measure themselves against the group’s other unbeaten team.
Spain confirmed lineup
Luis De La Fuente sets Spain up in a 4-2-3-1 with Unai Simón in goal behind a back four of Marc Pubill, Pau Cubarsí, Aymeric Laporte and Marc Cucurella. Martín Zubimendi and Fabián Ruiz anchor midfield, giving Pedri license to drift forward and link with Lamine Yamal and Álex Baena either side of Mikel Oyarzabal up top. There are no absences listed, so De La Fuente can call on his first-choice group, with Yamal’s movement off the right likely to be a central outlet against England’s back line.
Spain confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Unai Simón, Marc Pubill, Marc Cucurella, Fabián Ruiz, Pau Cubarsí, Aymeric Laporte, Lamine Yamal, Martín Zubimendi, Mikel Oyarzabal, Mikel Merino, Álex Baena. Coach: Luis de la Fuente.
England confirmed lineup
Thomas Tuchel also lines England up in a 4-2-3-1, with James Trafford behind a defense of Jarell Quansah, Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Lewis Hall. Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson sit in front of the back four, freeing Jude Bellingham to push into the final third alongside Morgan Rogers and Anthony Gordon in support of Harry Kane. With no absences to account for, Tuchel has his preferred attacking unit available, and Bellingham’s ability to find pockets between the lines figures to be a key factor against Spain’s midfield pairing.
England confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): James Trafford, Ben White, Lewis Hall, Jude Bellingham, Ezri Konsa, Jarell Quansah, Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice, Harry Kane, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon. Coach: Thomas Tuchel.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement marks new low after Portugal drops out of FIFA’s top 5 following heavy defeat as new ranking position emerges
items.description:
The setback against Denmark has also had consequences beyond the pitch, raising fresh questions about Portugal’s standing among the world’s leading sides. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement has coincided with a difficult start to a new chapter for Portugal, with Jorge Jesus facing an early test as the national team attempts to move forward without its long-time captain. The setback against Denmark has also had consequences beyond the pitch, raising fresh questions about Portugal’s standing among the world’s leading sides.



Portugal endured a disappointing evening on Saturday, suffering a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark at the Braga Municipal Stadium. The encounter marked the national team’s first appearance since Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, bringing an end to one of the most successful careers in international soccer.



Denmark took control shortly before half-time when Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg converted a penalty in the 43rd minute. Rasmus Hojlund then struck twice in the opening stages of the second half, scoring in the 50th and 57th minutes, before Joachim Andersen added a fourth in the 75th minute.



Bernardo Silva managed to score a late consolation goal in stoppage time, but the Selecao could not prevent a heavy defeat on home soil. The result was particularly disappointing for Jesus, whose first match in this new era ended with Portugal suffering one of their most damaging recent setbacks.









Ronaldo’s departure marks beginning of new era



The defeat came just days after Ronaldo officially brought his 23-year international career to a close, having represented Portugal 234 times and scored a record 146 goals. The 41-year-old leaves behind an extraordinary legacy, having captained the national team to Euro 2016 and further international success in the UEFA Nations League.



His departure also creates a significant leadership gap for Jesus, who must now build a team capable of competing without the forward who defined Portugal’s attacking identity for more than two decades. Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs wore a redesigned No. 7 shirt against Denmark, paying tribute to the number Ronaldo made famous during his international career.



Tempo de estrear um novo 7. Porque há um que será eterno ∞🐐 pic.twitter.com/UCozRU3t89— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 14, 2026 



The transition is particularly meaningful given that Ronaldo’s son has also started making his own way through Portugal’s youth ranks. Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. recently made his Portugal U17 debut, offering a glimpse of the next generation as his father’s senior international journey comes to an end.



Portugal falls in the provisional FIFA rankings



The consequences of the defeat were immediately reflected in the provisional FIFA Men’s World Rankings, where Portugal dropped two places from fifth to seventh. The national team lost 10.09 ranking points, taking its total down to 1,797.60, with Brazil moving into sixth place.



Portugal in new FIFA rankings



The movement also allowed Morocco to return to the top five, climbing to fifth position with 1,805.34 points. The Atlas Lions had already benefited from Brazil’s 3-2 defeat to Japan before Portugal’s loss to Denmark confirmed their latest improvement.



The updated provisional top seven consists of Spain, Argentina, France, England, Morocco, Brazil and Portugal. However, these positions remain subject to FIFA’s next official update, scheduled for November 18, 2026.
